In this experiment, you are to find the position of the centre of mass of an object.
Record all of your observations and answers on page 4 of the Answer Booklet.
Carry out the following instructions, referring to Fig. 2.1.
You are provided with a shaped sample of plasticine. Do not change its shape.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Place the metre rule on the pivot so that the 50.0 cm mark is directly over the pivot.

content.text: Place the metre rule on the pivot so that the 50.0 cm mark is directly over the pivot.

parts.label: b
parts.text:
Place the 50 g mass on the metre rule so that its centre is at the 30.0 cm mark. Record the
distance x from the 30 cm mark to the pivot.

content.html: Place the 50 g mass on the metre rule so that its centre is at the 30.0 cm mark. Record the distance x from the 30 cm mark to the pivot.

parts.label: c
parts.text:
Place the plasticine on the metre rule with the thickest end nearer the pivot (see Fig. 2.1).
Move the plasticine until the rule balances (do not change the position of the 50 g mass or the
pivot). Measure and record the distance ybetween the pivot and the end of the plasticine
nearer the pivot (see Fig. 2.1).

mark_scheme.label: 2(c)
mark_scheme.text:
y value less than 25 cm
y value to nearest mm

parts.label: d
parts.text:
Calculate the distance d between the centre of mass of the plasticine and the pivot using the
equation
d = kx,
where k = 1.25.

parts.text:
Calculate the distance t between the thicker end of the plasticine and its centre of mass using
the equation
t = (d – y).

parts.label: f
parts.text:
Move the 50 g mass so that x= 30.0 cm. The pivot must still be at the 50.0 cm mark. Repeat
steps (c) – (e).

mark_scheme.label: 2(f)
mark_scheme.text:
x = 30 (cm)
y value in range 30.0 – 37.5 (cm)
d = 37.5 (cm) (allow e.c.f.)
all x, y, d consistently in mm, cm or m (unit stated at least once)
x, y d units stated every time
t value correct arith
t values within 0.5 cm of each other
